title: Forty-Two at Monte Rei
title_candidates: Four Closing Pars at Monte Rei
theme: Monte Rei, new to TEG and the third-hardest course it has ever played, passed the TEG 19 Trophy lead back and forth all afternoon before Jon Baker's 42 points took it clear.
opening_hook: TEG had never played Monte Rei before Sunday: a Nicklaus course in the hills above Tavira with water on eleven holes, and five and a bit shots harder for a TEG golfer than an average course. Five players left 135 shots over par on it.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker's 42 points at Monte Rei, built on three opening pars, surviving a seven at the par-3 seventh, and closed out with four straight pars for 14 points from the 15th
round_story.why_it_matters: The best round of the day by four points on the hardest course TEG has visited this week, and the round that turned a one-point Trophy lead into five with two rounds left. His gross 88 was the second-lowest of the day behind Gregg Williams.
round_story.shape: He opened with pars at the first, second and third for 10 points, then put a seven on the card at the 230-yard par-3 seventh and watched Gregg Williams take the lead. He was still only level with Williams standing on the 15th tee. Four pars from the 15th, worth 14 points, took him to 42 for the round and 81 for the TEG 19 Trophy, five clear.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker Closes with Four Pars
Jon Baker Comes Home in Pars
round_story.chosen_headline: Jon Baker Closes with Four Pars
round_story.standfirst: The seventh cost him a seven and the lead, and he still played the last four holes in par figures for 14 points.

race_story.subject: The day from the vantage of those who lost ground: Gregg Williams twice held the Trophy lead and finished five behind, Alex Baker slid from one off the lead to fourteen, and John Patterson's 25 points opened a nine-point gap at the bottom
race_story.why_it_matters: Nobody's name changed at the top of any of the three competitions, yet every margin moved. Williams keeps the TEG 19 Green Jacket lead by four shots with the lowest gross round in both rounds so far; the Wooden Spoon gap went from level to nine in a single afternoon.
race_story.shape: Williams birdied the third after two opening bogeys and had the Trophy lead at the seventh, lost it at the twelfth, took it back at the thirteenth, and was overtaken for good at the sixteenth. He signed for 38 points and a gross 87, the lowest of the day, which left him leading the Jacket by four and trailing the Trophy by five. Behind them Alex Baker went from second to third and John Patterson, who bled 12 shots between the 11th and the 15th, is now nine points adrift at the foot of the Spoon.
headline_candidates: The Trophy Lead Changes Hands Four Times
Gregg Williams Keeps Hold of the Jacket
Nine Clear at the Wrong End
race_story.chosen_headline: The Trophy Lead Changes Hands Four Times
race_story.standfirst: Gregg Williams had it at the seventh and again at the thirteenth, scored 38 points, and still went to bed five behind.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker's 114 at Monte Rei: nines at the first and second, a ten at the par-3 seventh, a birdie at the eighth, an eight at the seventeenth, and a fall from second to third in the Trophy
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The ten at the seventh is the worst score Alex Baker has made on a par 3 in TEG. He dropped 14 shots in the first four holes alone, scored 29 points, and went from one point off the Trophy lead to fourteen behind it.
discovered_storylines.shape: He began with a nine at the first and a nine at the second, and had lost 14 shots to par by the fourth tee. The 230-yard seventh took ten, and he birdied the par-5 eighth immediately afterwards, then took nine points from the 12th, 13th and 14th. An eight at the seventeenth finished the card at 114.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Takes Ten at the Seventh
Fourteen Shots Gone in Four Holes
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Alex Baker Takes Ten at the Seventh
discovered_storylines.standfirst: His worst par-3 score in TEG, and one hole later he made a birdie at the eighth.

discovered_storylines.subject: Monte Rei's five par 5s and the 18 shots David Mullin and John Patterson gave away on four of them
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The holes that normally bring in points did the opposite. Patterson took ten at both the sixth and the eighteenth, and Mullin took nine at the sixth and nine at the sixteenth, between them costing 18 shots on four holes.
discovered_storylines.shape: The sixth, where huge bunkers sit in front of an offset green, took a ten from Patterson and a nine from Mullin. Mullin then ran up a nine at the par-5 sixteenth before birdieing the last. Patterson finished with a ten at the eighteenth, the short par 5 that curls round the lake.
headline_candidates: Tens at the Sixth and Eighteenth
Eighteen Shots Lost on Four Holes
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Tens at the Sixth and Eighteenth
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Monte Rei has five par 5s, and David Mullin and John Patterson contrived to drop 18 shots on four of them.

race_state_note: Two rounds remain. Jon Baker has had the best Stableford round in both rounds so far, and Gregg Williams the lowest gross in both; the Wooden Spoon gap went from level to nine points in one day.
